pr_title: feat(network): expose network events via browser context
pr_body:
+ fix #6340 
+ Exposes all the network related events (request, response, requestfailed, requestfinished) through the browser context to allow for managing network activity even if the is any navigations through popups or to new tabs which could result in creation of multiple page objects.
pr_comments: @dgozman WDYT of the above approach? Can i go ahead and expose all `network` events (`requestfailed`, `requestfinishes`, `response`) if the approach feels good enough?
Force pushed to trigger the previously hanging CI builds.

issue_context.title: [Feature] Capture network requests on BrowserContext
comments: We can do something like `browserContext.on('request')` that captures requests from all the pages in the context.

@vigneshshanmugam CDP works per-target, so such an API on the context will not match the internals and I don't think we should do something like this. Note that you can use [`newBrowserCDPSession()`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-chromiumbrowser#chromiumbrowsernewbrowsercdpsession) and manually attach to all pages inside it.

If you are willing to contribute `browserContext.on('request')`, that would be wonderful!

> Gotcha, that makes sense. I tried working through `newBrowserCDPSession`, is it possible to use the playwright API instead of manually dealing with browser targets and creating sessions for each target - page creation? is there a better way to create the session using the playwright API using the `targetinfo.sessionid`.

Not really. We expose `CDPSession` for those who feel adventurous or have some tooling already built upon CDP. It is not cross-browser-compatible, so we are unlikely to build APIs on top of it. Instead, we prioritize features that help many users and implement them across all browsers.

> Totally, would like to take it for a spin.

Great! I'd start with `src/client/events.ts` and look around for the 'request' event. Let me know if you have any questions - happy to help.

> We expose CDPSession for those who feel adventurous or have some tooling already built upon CDP. It is not cross-browser-compatible, so we are unlikely to build APIs on top of it. 

Yeah can reason to that one. One of the reasons why we went with using CDP is because the `page.on(request)` event does get all of the details as per https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Network/#event-requestWillBeSent. Reason being we need those details to get the blocking, queued and other timing info required to construct the waterfall appropriately which is what `request` event lack and went with CDP instead. Is there a possibility to expose that information at some point? 

> Great! I'd start with src/client/events.ts and look around for the 'request' event. Let me know if you have any questions - happy to help.

Sure, thanks 👍

> It would be really cool, if playwright can expose the original unmodified event as second argument to the `request` event which would eliminate the extra browser session handling that we discussed before. Happy to do a PR as well. Let me know if would work for the playwright team

This is not going to work, because it's not cross-browser. However, we can expose additional information if you need something, directly on the `Request` object. Please file a separate issue for that, and we'll triage/prioritize it accordingly.

> his is not going to work, because it's not cross-browser. However, we can expose additional information if you need something, directly on the Request object. Please file a separate issue for that, and we'll triage/prioritize it accordingly.

sure, will create a separate issue to expose some more information from the raw events.

Ahh i get it, its for the server side stuff? I brought them back, but we can move to BrowserContext.Request in another PR to make sure we dont miss our requests with HAR when popups are involved.
